category: hosted real-device and browser test farm

free_tier.stated: A one-time trial of 1,000 device minutes, or 250 device minutes as the standard allowance; the trial does not renew, and usage after it is USD 0.17 per device minute.
free_tier.notes: The pricing page notes that 1,000 minutes is a limited-time trial in place of the standard 250 minutes, and the FAQ states that the trial is one-time and does not renew.

per_object_cap.stated: Uploaded app or test archives are capped at 4 GB; generated video and device logs are each truncated at 1 GB and cumulative artifacts at 4 GB
per_object_cap.notes: The 4 GB figure is the per-file upload cap; artifact totals above 4 GB may drop video, logs or custom artifacts.

retention.stated: Apps and test packages are automatically removed after 30 days; logs, video recordings and other artifacts are stored 400 days; devices are cleaned between sessions and data can persist in some cases.
retention.notes: The 30 days applies to uploaded apps and test packages, not to test artifacts, which are kept 400 days.

egress.terms: All devices have internet connectivity over WiFi; traffic to internal systems can be allow-listed from 54.244.50.32-54.244.50.63, and device traffic is shaped by a chosen network profile. No separate per-GB egress price is published; device minutes are the meter.

interface_detail: A console for scheduling runs and remote access, an HTTPS API with AWS SDKs, a Jenkins plug-in and a Gradle plug-in; Appium, XCTest/XCUITest and instrumentation frameworks drive the devices.
tooling: the AWS console, AWS CLI purchase-offering and list-offerings commands, the Device Farm API and AWS SDKs, a Jenkins plug-in and a Gradle plug-in; Device Connect bridges local adb to devices in us-west-2.
chaining: A CI job uploads an app and test package, schedules a run over a device pool and downloads reports, screenshots and video; because uploaded packages are removed after 30 days, results that must outlive that window need a separate storage record.

limits.value: at most 5 devices tested simultaneously by default on metered use; remote-access concurrency quota is 2 and metered concurrency can be raised on request
a 150-minute hard limit on an automated test run and on a remote access session
a maximum of 250 in-flight jobs per account, a soft limit; runs remain queued at most 24 hours
4 GB maximum app upload, with video and device logs truncated at 1 GB each
iOS simulators always bill metered and cannot use unmetered slots; an account must be approved to purchase the requested number of device slots

limits_note: Unmetered plans start at USD 250.00 per device slot per month, priced per usage type and device family; private devices start at USD 200 a month; desktop browser tests are USD 0.005 per instance minute.
binding_note: The 1,000 trial device minutes are consumed in parallel across devices, so the default concurrency of five devices running for up to 150 minutes each spends a long run fastest; concurrency and the per-run 150-minute cap bind before the file size caps.

identity_cost.detail: An AWS account needs a root email address and a phone number verified by SMS, and the advanced sign-up requires a valid payment method before it can proceed; Device Farm further needs an IAM user with permission and the service is available only in us-west-2. Private device and slot purchases are billed to that account.

reliability_note: Test runs and remote sessions end at 150 minutes, runs queued over 24 hours are dropped, iOS apps are re-signed with a wildcard profile which removes several entitlements, and data can persist between sessions in some cases.
confidence_note: The price, trial and plan floors come from the provider pricing page and FAQ read 2026-11-24; limits from the developer guide, identity from the AWS sign-up docs, and egress from the FAQ and device support page.
